\begin{chapteropening}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{نفوذ} (nufūdh)}{نفوذ (nufūdh)}]{\ar{نفوذ} (nufūdh) — influence}

\label{lesson:AR-C389-nufudh}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to violate, then the Arabic for to exploit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{نفوذ}}
\textbf{\ar{نفوذ}} — \emph{nufūdh} — \textquotedblleft{}influence\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{لهذا} \ar{الرجل} \ar{نفوذ} \ar{كبير} \ar{في} \ar{المدينة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{li-hādhā ar-rajul nufūdh kabīr fī al-madīna.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This man has great influence in the city.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{نفوذ}} (\emph{nufūdh}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{n-f-dh}, \textquotedblleft{}to pass through, to pierce\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Nufūdh} is passing through: the power to make things happen, influence.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nufūdh}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nufūdh}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{li-hādhā ar-rajul nufūdh kabīr fī al-madīna.} — This man has great influence in the city.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to violate, then the Arabic for to exploit, then say \emph{nufūdh} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{نفوذ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Influence\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ساد} (sāda)}{ساد (sāda)}]{\ar{ساد} (sāda) — to prevail}

\label{lesson:AR-C389-sada-prevail}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to exploit, then the Arabic for influence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ساد}}
\textbf{\ar{ساد}} — \emph{sāda} — \textquotedblleft{}to prevail\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{ساد} \ar{الخوف} \ar{في} \ar{المدينة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sāda al-khawf fī al-madīna.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Fear prevailed in the city.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يسود}, \emph{yasūd}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{ساد}} (\emph{sāda}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{s-w-d}, \textquotedblleft{}to be lord, to be chief\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Sāda} is a Form I verb, to be master: to rule, to prevail. \ar{سيد}, a lord, is from the same root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sāda}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sāda}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sāda al-khawf fī al-madīna.} — Fear prevailed in the city.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to exploit, then the Arabic for influence, then say \emph{sāda} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{ساد} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To prevail\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{انضم} (inḍamma)}{انضم (inḍamma)}]{\ar{انضم} (inḍamma) — to join}

\label{lesson:AR-C389-indamma}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for influence, then the Arabic for to prevail.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{انضم}}
\textbf{\ar{انضم}} — \emph{inḍamma} — \textquotedblleft{}to join\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{انضم} \ar{أخي} \ar{إلى} \ar{فريق} \ar{المدرسة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{inḍamma akhī ilā farīq al-madrasa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My brother joined the school team.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{ينضم}, \emph{yanḍamm}.

It takes \ar{إلى}: \ar{انضم} \ar{إلى} ….

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{انضم}} (\emph{inḍamma}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḍ-m-m}, \textquotedblleft{}to draw together\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form VII, to be drawn in with others: to join.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{inḍamma}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{inḍamma}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{inḍamma akhī ilā farīq al-madrasa.} — My brother joined the school team.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for influence, then the Arabic for to prevail, then say \emph{inḍamma} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أجبر} (ajbara)}{أجبر (ajbara)}]{\ar{أجبر} (ajbara) — to force}

\label{lesson:AR-C389-ajbara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to prevail, then the Arabic for to join.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أجبر}}
\textbf{\ar{أجبر}} — \emph{ajbara} — \textquotedblleft{}to force\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أجبر} \ar{المطر} \ar{الناس} \ar{على} \ar{البقاء} \ar{في} \ar{البيت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ajbara al-maṭar an-nās ʿalā al-baqāʾ fī al-bayt.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The rain forced people to stay at home.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يجبر}, \emph{yujbir}.

It takes \ar{على}: \ar{أجبره} \ar{على} ….

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أجبر}} (\emph{ajbara}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{j-b-r}, \textquotedblleft{}to set a broken bone\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form IV; Lane gives it for compelling someone: to force.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ajbara}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ajbara}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ajbara al-maṭar an-nās ʿalā al-baqāʾ fī al-bayt.} — The rain forced people to stay at home.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to prevail, then the Arabic for to join, then say \emph{ajbara} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{استقرار} (istiqrār)}{استقرار (istiqrār)}]{\ar{استقرار} (istiqrār) — stability}

\label{lesson:AR-C389-istiqrar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to join, then the Arabic for to force.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{استقرار}}
\textbf{\ar{استقرار}} — \emph{istiqrār} — \textquotedblleft{}stability\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{يحتاج} \ar{الأطفال} \ar{إلى} \ar{الاستقرار}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yaḥtāju al-aṭfāl ilā al-istiqrār.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Children need stability.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{استقرار}} (\emph{istiqrār}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{q-r-r}, \textquotedblleft{}to settle, to be still\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Istiqrār} is the Form X verbal noun, settling in place: stability.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\section[(dialogue)]{Words from chapters 382–389 — a review}

\label{lesson:AR-R389-review-382-389}



\begin{quote}
Say the Arabic for a protest and dignity.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a protest, dignity, to demonstrate, to protest, a strike
  \item the economy, a tax, a deficit, inflation, to invest
  \item to fund, to allocate, industry, agriculture, development
  \item an organization, an association, a trade union, a council, a member
  \item to cooperate, to negotiate, to ratify, a conflict, a crisis
  \item migration, a nation, nationality, a majority, a minority
  \item corruption, a bribe, reform, to violate, to exploit
  \item influence, to prevail, to join, to force, stability
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A protest? (\textbf{\ar{احتجاج}}, \emph{iḥtijāj}.) Dignity? (\textbf{\ar{كرامة}}, \emph{karāma}.) To demonstrate? (\textbf{\ar{تظاهر}}, \emph{taẓāhara}.) To protest? (\textbf{\ar{احتج}}, \emph{iḥtajja}.) A strike? (\textbf{\ar{إضراب}}, \emph{iḍrāb}.) The economy? (\textbf{\ar{اقتصاد}}, \emph{iqtiṣād}.) A tax? (\textbf{\ar{ضريبة}}, \emph{ḍarība}.) A deficit? (\textbf{\ar{عجز}}, \emph{ʿajz}.) Inflation? (\textbf{\ar{تضخم}}, \emph{taḍakhkhum}.) To invest? (\textbf{\ar{استثمر}}, \emph{istathmara}.) To fund? (\textbf{\ar{مول}}, \emph{mawwala}.) To allocate? (\textbf{\ar{خصص}}, \emph{khaṣṣaṣa}.) Industry? (\textbf{\ar{صناعة}}, \emph{ṣināʿa}.) Agriculture? (\textbf{\ar{زراعة}}, \emph{zirāʿa}.) Development? (\textbf{\ar{تنمية}}, \emph{tanmiya}.) An organization? (\textbf{\ar{منظمة}}, \emph{munaẓẓama}.) An association? (\textbf{\ar{جمعية}}, \emph{jamʿiyya}.) A trade union? (\textbf{\ar{نقابة}}, \emph{niqāba}.) A council? (\textbf{\ar{مجلس}}, \emph{majlis}.) A member? (\textbf{\ar{عضو}}, \emph{ʿuḍw}.) To cooperate? (\textbf{\ar{تعاون}}, \emph{taʿāwana}.) To negotiate? (\textbf{\ar{تفاوض}}, \emph{tafāwaḍa}.) To ratify? (\textbf{\ar{صادق}}, \emph{ṣādaqa}.) A conflict? (\textbf{\ar{صراع}}, \emph{ṣirāʿ}.) A crisis? (\textbf{\ar{أزمة}}, \emph{azma}.) Migration? (\textbf{\ar{هجرة}}, \emph{hijra}.) A nation? (\textbf{\ar{أمة}}, \emph{umma}.) Nationality? (\textbf{\ar{جنسية}}, \emph{jinsiyya}.) A majority? (\textbf{\ar{أغلبية}}, \emph{aghlabiyya}.) A minority? (\textbf{\ar{أقلية}}, \emph{aqalliyya}.) Corruption? (\textbf{\ar{فساد}}, \emph{fasād}.) A bribe? (\textbf{\ar{رشوة}}, \emph{rashwa}.) Reform? (\textbf{\ar{إصلاح}}, \emph{iṣlāḥ}.) To violate? (\textbf{\ar{انتهك}}, \emph{intahaka}.) To exploit? (\textbf{\ar{استغل}}, \emph{istaghalla}.) Influence? (\textbf{\ar{نفوذ}}, \emph{nufūdh}.) To prevail? (\textbf{\ar{ساد}}, \emph{sāda}.) To join? (\textbf{\ar{انضم}}, \emph{inḍamma}.) To force? (\textbf{\ar{أجبر}}, \emph{ajbara}.) Stability? (\textbf{\ar{استقرار}}, \emph{istiqrār}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
